sentences.text: Task 3. Charlie and Greta are making a YouTube video at an exhibition at Bolin Medicine’s factory in Hong Kong.
Listen to their conversation and complete the information in the spaces below.
low. You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
I can’t believe we're finally here at the Bolin Medicine factory exhibition.
Bolin medicine is only the most popular medicine for children in Hong Kong.
I’ve had their medicine tin box at home since I was a kid.
Uh, OK, so it’s for children.
What kind of medicine is it?
Is it like those sweets for a sore throat?
No, I know which ones your talk.
talking about but not them.
My mum would give it to me every time I had a high temperature.
It really worked.
It would help me sleep better as well when I was struggling to get to sleep.
Now that you come to mention it, I seem to vaguely remember my mum giving it to me too.
here. But it gave me a stomach ache, so I wasn’t a big fan of it.
So now you know why I'm so excited.
I can’t wait to learn more about their manufacturing process.
I was reading that they won the Shona Finances Award last year.
What’s that? Because they are successful with the finances and make a huge profit?
Well they do make a huge profit, that’s true but shown the Finances are just the Sponsors of the award.
It’s meant to look beyond just profits.
It’s one of those international awards like one of those, Environmental Excellence awards.
So, it’s for being environmentally friendly or using natural products or something?
No, no it’s an award for companies that help their society.
So, Bo Lin have this campaign to employ all types of people in Hong Kong society to help them: people over 65, people with disabilities, single parents, newly arrived immigrants, that sort of thing.
So that’s why they won the Shona.
Well, good for them.
And apparently their manufacturing processes are of the highest standard.
Let’s start right away then.
Look! This exhibit hears about the first step in the process sourcing of ingredients, Okay, OK, so it says here that they use quality local suppliers for the ingredients.
No wonder they are so successful.
Nothing beats quality local suppliers if you ask me.
True. And apparently, they say that because of that they can ensure their raw ingredients does not come in contact with banned substances during this step.
I wonder what band substances mean.
Band substances? I don’t know.
I doubt it would be turmeric or ginseng or anything like that.
Lots of these companies have been busy promoting them as miracle cures for everything.
I read somewhere that some companies use pearls.
Well, that does sound quite a controversial ingredient.
Well, that’s what I was thinking or maybe one of those problematic ingredients like shark fin, but no, it says here that it’s the good old peanut which is banned.
There are too many children who have peanut allergy these days and they want their medicine to be more accessible.
Anyways, let’s move on to the next exhibit.
It’s about the preparation stage.
OK, so it says here that this is where they grind and measure ingredients to prepare them for further processing.
That’s why it says that there are a number of conditions they keep an eye on.
The first condition they need to maintain is room temperature.
temperature. Apparently, that is to avoid any damage.
Like they wouldn’t want to burn or freeze the ingredients.
That makes sense.
I'm assuming the ingredients are quite delicate.
OK, let’s see.
It says here that the next condition they need to ensure is low humidity.
It’s important to control humidity to prevent mold.
Don’t tell me about that.
I hate even thinking about mould.
It’s gross! Oops, sorry about that.
And it says that the third condition they need to maintain is high air pressure.
They do this to kill bacteria.
You keep reading that, Charlie.
All this talk of mould and bacteria’s making me feel uncomfortable.
I think I will go ahead to the next exhibit and read about the processing stage.
Let’s go together.
So what process is involved in making bowl in medicine?
Believe it or not, it says here that it’s cold brew.
Cold brew for medicine?
That’s something I’ve never heard of.
Apparently, it helps maintain the freshness and flavour.
I'm sure it does.
Hey, look at this.
We’re at the last step already.
It’s packaging. Every Hong Kong parent’s favourite part of bowling Medicine.
That was quick.
It Shows how efficient the factory is at producing medicine.
And they’re well aware of it.
They stopped using tin boxes for packaging a few years back.
Now they make sure it’s environmentally friendly.
Helps to showcase them as a caring company.
Look at the packaging design too.
It’s obviously trying to evoke feelings of family.
and, you know, comfort and warmth.
That’s why you anyway, thanks for joining us at the Bowlin Medicine Factory.
